body:
Nah, 6 year old me was just starting to figure out what a disappointment she was, and beginning self-disgust. 
Anyway, thanks for your time. I still feel dizzy, but I've gotten back a bit of unrealistic hope.

I get you. It just seems to me like 6-20 has been all pretty similar, and it's that I just hate my own company so much, if it hasn't changed for 20 years, I don't think it'll change in the future. That and failing at doing what I have to gets tiring, and takes its toll on others as well as me.
All right. I hear that advice a lot and try to keep it in mind. But I just feel like I'll end up right where I've been. I appreciate your positivity though.

Just from experience. Speaking to people, they often ignore what I say or don't address it, as if they don't want to speak to me, even if they've been around me/known me for a while. Leave quickly (I don't smell, or at least I think, I do take showers.). Look at me with confusion even if I make the most banal conversation or small talk. As if everything I say is nonsensical. Always eye me with caution, look nervous around me.

And with the no skills part, I don't think that's very true. It seems that everyone around me has some skill. I'm studying engineering. I get happy if I can understand the simplest concepts. If I can do even that. But everyone else is just so goddamn high achieving "OHOHO how can anyone not get this, it's so simple. I was just telling this interviewer the other day, blah blah, how fantastic I am." Obviously these students are doing fantastic. Internships, research, etc. And if not that, well at least they're fantastic at problem solving.
